translate_en|mods/CameraMotionBlur/42/me: Out of a dark place into bright light (a dark house onto a sunny street, a night street into a lit room): for a moment everything is too bright, washed out and pale, and it settles in about two seconds. From bright light into the dark: everything is darker and almost colourless for a while, and the eyes get used to it slowly, in 15-20 seconds. A tired or drunk character adapts more slowly. Loading, sleeping and fast forward do not trigger it. The interface stays as it is. 100 is the default, 0 turns it off, 200 doubles it.
Your character's eyes get used to the light: too bright for a moment after the dark, too dark for a while after bright light.

When the frame rate stays under the lowest FPS below, the mod lowers its heaviest effects one step at a time and checks that the frame rate really got better. When there is room again, it raises them back. Only the look of the mod changes, never the game.

Autofocus follows where your character looks, like the game's vision cone (a driver backing up looks back). Like the game's vision cone - the sharp area is exactly as wide as what your character can see and changes with it: wider in daylight and in a car, narrower at night, in dark rooms, when tired, drunk or panicking. Fixed angle - always the angle set above. Everything inside stays untouched while running, driving and zooming, including people, cars and fences standing there; the blur fades in just outside.
Keeps everything your character can see sharp: the blur shows only outside the field of view.

Nothing around your character, growing towards the screen edges and strongest in the corners. Done on the finished colours, so it shows at night too. Normally slight. Stronger when the picture moves fast (running, sprinting, driving) and when your character feels bad (pain, drink, panic, tiredness). Changes smoothly. The interface stays clean. 100 is the default, 0 turns it off, 200 doubles it.
Red and blue drift slightly apart towards the screen edges, like a real lens.
Everything nearer than the aim point
The way to the aim point

Depth of field works while aiming with the mouse. The focus follows the aiming reticle smoothly and fades in and out. The way to the aim point - a band from your character to the reticle stays sharp, wider near the target; everything else blurs. Everything nearer than the aim point - a circle around your character out to the reticle stays sharp, everything farther blurs. Blur amount above scales this too.
While your character aims, the way to the aim point stays sharp and everything behind it and around blurs.

Turns the whole mod on or off: motion blur, depth of field, camera shake, film grain, chromatic aberration, lens flare and glowing signs, eye adaptation and the VHS camcorder mode. Off - the picture is exactly the game's own.
The faint coloured spots that float across the screen when the camera moves (the six brightest lights throw them). Off: every light keeps its glow and its streak, the floating reflections are gone.

From street lamps, lamps, fires, stoves, vehicle lights and flashlights you can see - placed right on the bulb or flame the game draws, and on the head and tail lamps of every vanilla vehicle. Every light on the screen glows - a lamp in the shape of its shade or tube, a street lamp in the shape of its globe, a stove or a fire in the shape of its flame - and the six brightest also throw reflections. The reflections float: they trail behind when the camera moves and drift slowly; with the camera further away the glow is bigger and the streak longer and thicker, closer - smaller, shorter and thinner; while zooming the streak stretches for a moment. Signs, lit and painted, glow in their own shape and colours - the brighter the sign, the more (a neon sign, a sign under a street lamp). Headlights and flashlights flare only when they shine towards the camera. Strong at night, barely there by day. A tired, drunk or hurt character sees more glare. The interface stays clean. The reflections have their own tick box: off, the glow and the streak stay. 100 is the default, 0 turns it off, 200 doubles it.
Bright lights glow, throw a thin streak and faint coloured reflections across the screen, like in a real camera lens. Lamps and signs glow in their own shape and colours.

Normally very weak, fine and grey. Tired, panicking, drunk, hurt - stronger and coarser; calm and rested - almost invisible. In the dark (night outside, a dark room) - stronger, a little coarser and coloured, like a camera with too little light; in sunshine or under a lamp it fades back. Changes smoothly. The interface never gets grain. 100 is the default, 0 turns it off, 200 doubles it.
Living film grain on the world picture: barely visible normally, stronger in the dark and when your character feels bad.

Blur amount - how strong all the blur is: 0 turns it off, 100 is full. Blur quality - how smooth long streaks look; higher quality takes more work from the video card, the difference shows mostly when driving fast. Standing and walking cost nothing at any quality.
Write performance numbers to the log
Every 5 seconds one line with the FPS, the CPU and GPU time and the mod's own time goes to console.txt. Useful for a bug report. Off by default.

Log detail: Minimal writes only errors. Normal writes a few lines when the game loads and when something changes. Detailed also writes status lines every few seconds and many lines while the eyes adapt or the zoom changes; use it only when asked for a log.Auto performance: when the FPS stays under the lowest FPS you set, the mod lowers its heaviest effects one step at a time (glow of signs and lamps, lens reflections, blur quality, colour split) and checks that the FPS really got better. If it did not, the mod goes back, because it is not the cause. When the FPS is well above that number for a while, the effects come back. Blur quality 'Automatic' starts lower on a bigger screen. A line in console.txt tells every change.

Running - a light bob in step with the stride; sprinting - about twice as much; it follows the real speed and stops when you stand or run into a wall. Driving - a fine vibration from 40 km/h that grows up to 140 km/h. Only the picture of the world moves: the interface, the aiming reticle and the game's camera stay still. 100 is the default, 0 turns that part off, 200 doubles it.
The picture bobs in step while running and sprinting, and vibrates in a fast car.

Each kind of blur on its own, in percent: 100 is the default, 0 turns that part off. Camera movement - streaks when the picture slides (running, driving, looking around); walking stays sharp. Zoom - blur outwards from your character while the zoom changes. Running and Driving - extra speed blur towards the screen edges; in a car it grows with speed. Your character always stays sharp.
Blur depends on how the character feels
Influence of the character's state, percent

Makes the blur stronger and more solid when your character is very tired, out of breath, drunk, in pain, sick, panicking, starving or freezing/overheating (up to twice as strong), and a little lighter and slightly see-through when they are well rested, full of breath and in a good mood. Changes smoothly over about a second. Influence: 100 is the default, 0 turns it off, 200 doubles it.
Tired, out of breath, drunk, hurt, sick or panicking - more blur; rested and in a good mood - a little less.
Works only when the game runs with -debug: red shows where motion blur is allowed, blue shows where the depth of field blurs while aiming.
Hides the whole game interface while recording (V shows it again).
Turns the VHS camcorder look on and off. Home by default. With -debug the game itself takes F2, F7, F8 and F9 (its editors), so those keys will not work here.
REC, the counter and the battery, time and date, the air temperature where your character is, the street (or the building, or a place from the map) and the town - in the glowing VCR OSD Mono letters.
VHS: the game's sound stutters too
On a worn tape the glitches cut up not only the tape's own sound but also the game's sound effects, music and engines - for a fraction of a second, in time with the picture.

Press the key (Home by default) to film your character on an old home video tape: soft picture, bleeding colours, shaking lines, tracking bands, tape noise, the camcorder display with a blinking REC, the game's time, date and temperature, the street and the town you are in. The tape gets more worn as your character's health drops: near death the picture falls apart, the letters float, colours fade and turn wrong, the frame jumps and rolls. The tape is heard too: hiss, the camcorder's motor, buzz and crackle growing with wear, the sound stuttering with the picture. Motion blur, depth of field, film grain, colour split and eye adaptation rest while recording. Letters: VCR OSD Mono by Riciery Leal. 100 is the default, 0 is a clean tape, 200 doubles the wear.
